Use Tier 2 architectural deepening: add a learned long-term preference branch to SASRec while retaining its sequential backbone. Focus on model_design, with checkpoint and predictor compatibility handled in training_evaluation. Recency weighting reduced macro HR@10 from 0.5137 to 0.5062 and Electronics HR@10 from 0.410 to 0.375; this motivates testing whether explicitly preserving broader history helps, although it does not establish the cause of the decline. The hypothesis is that the current final-position representation does not consistently retain persistent user interests.

At each sequence position, compute the padding-masked cumulative mean of the existing item embeddings, using only items at or before that position. Project this pooled representation into the hidden dimension and combine it with the transformer representation through a learned elementwise sigmoid gate. Use the fused representation for both training logits and candidate prediction, retaining the existing item embeddings, learned item bias, uniform sampled-softmax loss, and 64-negative sampling. This is one controlled architectural change: restore uniform loss aggregation if starting from the recency-weighted attempt, and preserve all other training settings.

Save the added projection and gate parameters in each category checkpoint, and ensure the predictor writer loads the updated SASRec class so validation and host inference use identical fusion logic. Preserve all four dataset routes, supplied splits, seeds, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and single-GPU execution. Select checkpoints with the fixed validation protocol and assess the change using pinned host macro HR@10 and category results, without accessing test labels or claiming an improvement before evaluation.
